messages.content: Find an Italian restaurant near me in New York that provides vegetarian food options and a Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

function.name: restaurant_finder
function.description: Search for restaurants based on location, cuisine type and other preferences. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: City and state, e.g. New York, NY.

cuisine.description: Type of cuisine the user is interested in, e.g. Italian, Japanese etc.

preferences.description: Extra features in the restaurant. default is ['Delivery'].

The user wants two separate searches:

1. Find an Italian restaurant near them in New York that provides vegetarian food options.

2. Find a Japanese sushi restaurant in Los Angeles that offers delivery service.

We need to call the function twice with appropriate arguments.

First call: location: "New York, NY", cuisine: "Italian", preferences: ["Vegetarian"] (or maybe include Delivery? The requirement says "provides vegetarian food options". So we set preferences to ["Vegetarian"]. The function signature expects preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[], but it's ambiguous: It might accept array or single string? The description says preferences?: "Vegetarian" | "Delivery" | "Vegan" | "Takeout"[]; That seems like it can be either a string or an array. We'll pass array ["Vegetarian"].

Second call: location: "Los Angeles, CA", cuisine: "Japanese", preferences: ["Delivery"].

We'll output the results after calling the function.
